chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both together from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from one of them, peace be upon them, who said:
I said to him: A man does not know whether he prayed one rak'ah or two? He said: “He repeats.”

key_terms.صَلَّى: he prayed; referring to the performance of salat (prayer)
key_terms.عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ: peace be upon them; honorific for the Imam
key_terms.لَا يَدْرِي: he does not know; indicating uncertainty in the prayer
key_terms.يُعِيدُ: he repeats; meaning the prayer must be performed again

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone doubts whether he prayed one rak'ah or two in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding doubt in salat (prayer). If a person does not know whether he has prayed one rak'ah or two, he must repeat the prayer.
